body:
> I see three possible solutions:
> 
> 1. call `set_base(light)` in the `Light3D` constructor
> 2. add and expose a new `RID get_light()` method
> 3. override `get_base()` to return `light`

`set_base` is already being called e.g. in `MeshInstance3D` or `SpriteBase3D`, so `1.` seems more consistent.

---

I've searched for `instance_set_base`, seems there's the same issue in `Decal`, `ReflectionProbe`, `VoxelGI` (for all of them `VisualInstance3D::base` end up not being set):
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6fd949a6dcbda94140200633394f2b4b99de8f6f/scene/3d/decal.cpp#L286
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6fd949a6dcbda94140200633394f2b4b99de8f6f/scene/3d/reflection_probe.cpp#L306
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6fd949a6dcbda94140200633394f2b4b99de8f6f/scene/3d/voxel_gi.cpp#L271-L274

> `set_base` is already being called e.g. in `MeshInstance3D` or `SpriteBase3D`, so `1.` seems more consistent

And it actually works.

Personally, I don't like `set_base()` in `Light3D`. Nothing stops you from calling `set_base()` outside the `Light3D` constructor (for example, from GDScript) and clearing the base again.
With `MeshInstance3D`, it is called when you change the mesh resource. As far as I know, it is not supposed to change the light type.

I think `Light3D`, `Decal`, `ReflectionProbe`, and `VoxelGI` intentionally have their own dedicated `light`, `decal`, `probe`, and other properties, so they are not overridden by `set_base()`

I think we need to look at the history a little bit and see if non-mesh types were purposefully excluded from calling `set_base()`

In general, we definitely want to discourage users from mixing RenderingServer calls with Scene-level calls. You can easily break a node by changing its base. However, that is already possible since `get_instance` and `get/set_base` are exposed. 

In general it seems that `set_base()` is used by types that will have their base changed at run time (Mesh types, Sprite3D, Lightmap, LightOccluder, etc.)

However, from a quick look I see that FogVolume, CPUParticles, and VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D all use `set_base()` despite not needed to be set at run time. So I think more likely the `set_base()` API was added and just not used consistently. So it would be worth doing a search through the git history and see if thats the case

_edit: Looks like at one point `set_base()` did nothing but call `instance_set_base`, so it was random if it was used or if `instance_set_base` was called directly. Here is the commit adding get_base https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/33a0011ab292214cee81363bbb50d9de123af825_

based on that, I would go with Kleonc's suggestion and just use `set_base()`

Ok, I’ve looked at the history, and `Light3D` has used its own `light` property from the very beginning https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/0b806ee0fc9097fa7bda7ac0109191c9c5e0a1ac
`set_base` has been there since the initial commit. `RID base` and `get_base` were added much later
